title: QUIC Version 2 Static Floor (RFC 9369)
purpose: Capture the RFC 9369 QUIC v2 wire-format and cryptographic floor that is already implemented in the transport helpers.
scope: This specification covers the RFC 9369 v2 version constant, long-header packet-type mapping, Initial salt and HKDF labels, and Retry integrity key/nonce. It does not cover the compatible-version runtime-selection follow-up from RFC 9368 or any higher-layer application adaptation for version negotiation.
context: RFC 9369 defines QUIC version 2 as a v1-compatible wire-format with new packet-type bits, new Initial keying material, and new Retry integrity values. The repository already has the version-aware helper surface for those static changes, while the full compatible-version runtime-selection flow remains in the RFC 9368 follow-up gap.

requirements.title: Recognize QUIC version 2 long headers
requirements.statement: An endpoint that supports QUIC version 2 MUST accept 0x6B3343CF as a supported transport version and use the version-specific bit assignments defined by RFC 9369 when encoding and decoding long-header packet types.

requirements.title: Use the RFC 9369 Initial salt and labels
requirements.statement: A QUIC v2 endpoint MUST derive and validate Initial packet protection using the RFC 9369 Initial salt and the `quicv2 key`, `quicv2 iv`, and `quicv2 hp` labels, keeping v1 and v2 Initial protection material distinct.

requirements.title: Use the RFC 9369 Retry integrity key and nonce
requirements.statement: A QUIC v2 endpoint MUST generate and validate Retry integrity tags using the RFC 9369 v2 Retry secret material, keeping Retry metadata bound to the version carried by the Retry packet.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This slice is intentionally narrow. It owns the QUIC v2 static floor: version recognition, packet-type mapping, Initial protection, and Retry integrity. It does not claim the compatible-version runtime-selection follow-up from RFC 9368 or any higher-layer adaptation beyond the transport helpers.
